views.name: races_with_pit_data
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT races_ext.race_id
FROM races_ext
JOIN pit_stops ON pit_stops.race_id = races_ext.race_id
views.description: Select the cohort of races that have pit stop data available (only these races are considered).

views.name: lap_position_pairs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lp_prev.race_id AS race_id,
  lp_curr.lap AS lap,
  lp_curr.driver_id AS driver_a_id,
  lp_curr_overtaken.driver_id AS driver_x_id,
  CASE WHEN lp_prev.position > lp_prev_overtaken.position THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS was_behind_prev_lap,
  CASE WHEN lp_curr.position > lp_curr_overtaken.position THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_behind_curr_lap,
  lp_prev.lap AS lap_prev,
  lp_curr.lap AS lap_curr,
  -- gap in seconds on current lap: difference in lap_times.milliseconds if available (positive means A is slower/behind)
  (CAST(lt_curr_overtaken.milliseconds AS INTEGER) - CAST(lt_curr.milliseconds AS INTEGER)) / 1000.0 AS gap_curr_seconds,
  (CAST(lt_prev_overtaken.milliseconds AS INTEGER) - CAST(lt_prev.milliseconds AS INTEGER)) / 1000.0 AS gap_prev_seconds,
  -- whether driver X had any pit_stop recorded on the current lap
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pit_stops ps_curr
    WHERE ps_curr.race_id = lp_curr.race_id
      AND ps_curr.driver_id = lp_curr_overtaken.driver_id
      AND ps_curr.lap = lp_curr.lap
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS x_pitted_on_curr_lap,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pit_stops ps_prev
    WHERE ps_prev.race_id = lp_prev.race_id
      AND ps_prev.driver_id = lp_prev_overtaken.driver_id
      AND ps_prev.lap = lp_prev.lap
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS x_pitted_on_prev_lap,
  -- whether driver X retired on the current lap (presence in retirements with matching lap)
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM retirements r_curr
    WHERE r_curr.race_id = lp_curr.race_id
      AND r_curr.driver_id = lp_curr_overtaken.driver_id
      AND CAST(r_curr.lap AS INTEGER) = lp_curr.lap
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS x_retired_on_curr_lap,
  -- race start lap flag: true if previous lap is 0 (indicative of starting grid) or prev lap is NULL
  CASE WHEN lp_prev.lap IS NULL OR lp_prev.lap = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_race_start_lap
FROM
  -- current lap positions (alias A is potential overtaker)
  lap_positions lp_curr
JOIN
  -- previous lap positions for same driver A (could be same race, previous lap number)
  lap_positions lp_prev
  ON lp_prev.race_id = lp_curr.race_id
  AND lp_prev.driver_id = lp_curr.driver_id
  AND lp_prev.lap = lp_curr.lap - 1
-- join to the overtaken driver X on same race/lap (pairing every other driver present on same lap)
JOIN
  lap_positions lp_curr_overtaken
  ON lp_curr_overtaken.race_id = lp_curr.race_id
  AND lp_curr_overtaken.lap = lp_curr.lap
  AND lp_curr_overtaken.driver_id != lp_curr.driver_id
LEFT JOIN
  lap_positions lp_prev_overtaken
  ON lp_prev_overtaken.race_id = lp_curr.race_id
  AND lp_prev_overtaken.driver_id = lp_curr_overtaken.driver_id
  AND lp_prev_overtaken.lap = lp_curr.lap - 1
-- join lap_times to derive millisecond gaps; prefer matching lap_times rows
LEFT JOIN
  lap_times lt_curr
  ON lt_curr.race_id = lp_curr.race_id
  AND lt_curr.driver_id = lp_curr.driver_id
  AND lt_curr.lap = lp_curr.lap
LEFT JOIN
  lap_times lt_curr_overtaken
  ON lt_curr_overtaken.race_id = lp_curr_overtaken.race_id
  AND lt_curr_overtaken.driver_id = lp_curr_overtaken.driver_id
  AND lt_curr_overtaken.lap = lp_curr_overtaken.lap
LEFT JOIN
  lap_times lt_prev
  ON lt_prev.race_id = lp_prev.race_id
  AND lt_prev.driver_id = lp_prev.driver_id
  AND lt_prev.lap = lp_prev.lap
LEFT JOIN
  lap_times lt_prev_overtaken
  ON lt_prev_overtaken.race_id = lp_prev_overtaken.race_id
  AND lt_prev_overtaken.driver_id = lp_prev_overtaken.driver_id
  AND lt_prev_overtaken.lap = lp_prev_overtaken.lap
views.description: For every race, lap, and pair of drivers (A overtaker, X overtaken), produce whether A was behind X on lap L-1 and whether A is behind X on lap L, plus timing/gap info and flags for race start; include retirements and pit entry/exit markers for driver X on those laps. This uses lap-by-lap relative positions, lap timestamps/gaps, and pit/retirement events to compute the transition from not-behind to behind between consecutive laps.

views.name: candidate_overtakes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lpp.race_id,
  lpp.lap AS lap,
  lpp.driver_a_id,
  lpp.driver_x_id,
  lpp.gap_curr_seconds,
  lpp.x_pitted_on_curr_lap,
  lpp.x_pitted_on_prev_lap,
  lpp.x_retired_on_curr_lap,
  lpp.is_race_start_lap
FROM lap_position_pairs lpp
JOIN races_with_pit_data rpd ON rpd.race_id = lpp.race_id
WHERE
  (lpp.was_behind_prev_lap = 0 OR lpp.lap_prev IS NULL)
  AND lpp.is_behind_curr_lap = 1
views.description: Filter lap_position_pairs to rows that represent overtaking events by the definition: A was NOT behind X on lap L-1 and IS behind X on lap L (including race-start laps where applicable). Keep only overtakes that occur in races with pit data.

views.name: classified_overtakes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.race_id,
  c.lap,
  c.driver_a_id,
  c.driver_x_id,
  CASE
    WHEN c.x_retired_on_curr_lap = 1 THEN 'R'
    WHEN (
         (c.x_pitted_on_curr_lap = 1)
         OR (c.x_pitted_on_prev_lap = 1)
         )
         AND c.gap_curr_seconds IS NOT NULL
         AND c.gap_curr_seconds > 0
         THEN 'P'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS overtake_type
FROM candidate_overtakes c
WHERE
  -- only keep overtakes that can be unambiguously classified as R or P
  CASE
    WHEN c.x_retired_on_curr_lap = 1 THEN 'R'
    WHEN (
         (c.x_pitted_on_curr_lap = 1)
         OR (c.x_pitted_on_prev_lap = 1)
         )
         AND c.gap_curr_seconds IS NOT NULL
         AND c.gap_curr_seconds > 0
         THEN 'P'
    ELSE NULL
  END IS NOT NULL
views.description: Classify each candidate overtake into type 'R' or 'P' using external rules: 'R' if the overtaken driver X retired on lap L; 'P' if X pitted on lap L (pit entry) OR X pitted on lap L-1 (pit exit) and the gap/timing makes the overtake plausibly due to a pit (use gap_curr_seconds and domain thresholds). Exclude candidate overtakes that cannot be unambiguously classified as R or P.

views.name: overtake_events_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- construct a stable overtake_id by concatenating race, lap, attacker, victim and gap if available
  (CAST(co.race_id AS TEXT) || '_' || CAST(co.lap AS TEXT) || '_' || CAST(co.driver_a_id AS TEXT) || '_' || CAST(co.driver_x_id AS TEXT) || '_' || COALESCE(CAST(co.gap_curr_seconds AS TEXT), 'nogap')) AS overtake_id,
  co.lap AS lap,
  NULL AS time,
  co.driver_a_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
  co.driver_x_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
  NULL AS event_notes,
  CASE WHEN co.is_race_start_lap = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_start_related_flag,
  NULL AS overtaken_pit_entry_time,
  NULL AS overtaken_pit_exit_time,
  CASE WHEN co.x_retired_on_curr_lap = 1 THEN co.lap ELSE NULL END AS overtaken_retirement_lap
FROM candidate_overtakes co

semantic_filters.lap_range: none (lap filtering applied in a later step)

views.description: Select the base set of overtaking events with associated metadata (lap number, time, overtaking driver, overtaken driver, event notes or flags indicating start-related, pit in/out timestamps or lap markers, and retirement indication). This is the raw cohort of candidate overtakes before classification or lap filtering.

views.name: overtake_events_lap1_5
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  overtake_id,
  lap,
  time,
  overtaking_driver_id,
  overtaken_driver_id,
  event_notes,
  is_start_related_flag,
  overtaken_pit_entry_time,
  overtaken_pit_exit_time,
  overtaken_retirement_lap
FROM overtake_events_raw
WHERE lap >= 1 AND lap <= 5
views.description: Filter the raw overtaking events down to those that occurred on laps 1 through 5 inclusive.

views.name: overtake_classification_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oer.overtake_id AS overtake_id,
  -- retired_on_same_lap: true if overtaken_retirement_lap equals the overtake lap (non-null)
  CASE WHEN oer.overtaken_retirement_lap IS NOT NULL AND oer.overtaken_retirement_lap = oer.lap THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS retired_on_same_lap,
  -- pit_related: true if not retired_on_same_lap AND there is either an explicit pit entry time on same lap
  -- or a pit exit time on same lap, or event_notes indicate pit, or overtaken_pit_entry_time/overtaken_pit_exit_time non-null for that lap
  CASE
    WHEN (oer.overtaken_retirement_lap IS NOT NULL AND oer.overtaken_retirement_lap = oer.lap) THEN 0
    WHEN (
        (oer.overtaken_pit_entry_time IS NOT NULL)
        OR (oer.overtaken_pit_exit_time IS NOT NULL)
        OR (oer.event_notes IS NOT NULL AND lower(oer.event_notes) LIKE '%pit%')
      ) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS pit_related,
  -- start_related: true if not retired_on_same_lap AND not pit_related AND explicit start flag set
  CASE
    WHEN (oer.overtaken_retirement_lap IS NOT NULL AND oer.overtaken_retirement_lap = oer.lap) THEN 0
    WHEN (
      ( (oer.overtaken_pit_entry_time IS NOT NULL)
        OR (oer.overtaken_pit_exit_time IS NOT NULL)
        OR (oer.event_notes IS NOT NULL AND lower(oer.event_notes) LIKE '%pit%')
      )
    ) THEN 0
    WHEN (oer.is_start_related_flag IS NOT NULL AND oer.is_start_related_flag != 0) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS start_related,
  -- on_track_candidate: true if none of the above flags apply
  CASE
    WHEN (oer.overtaken_retirement_lap IS NOT NULL AND oer.overtaken_retirement_lap = oer.lap) THEN 0
    WHEN (
        (oer.overtaken_pit_entry_time IS NOT NULL)
        OR (oer.overtaken_pit_exit_time IS NOT NULL)
        OR (oer.event_notes IS NOT NULL AND lower(oer.event_notes) LIKE '%pit%')
      ) THEN 0
    WHEN (oer.is_start_related_flag IS NOT NULL AND oer.is_start_related_flag != 0) THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS on_track_candidate
FROM overtake_events_lap1_5 oer
views.description: For each overtake (lap 1-5), compute boolean classification flags according to the external rules: retired_on_same_lap (R), pit_related (P) if pit entry on same lap or pit-exit timing implies pit-related overtake, start_related (explicit flag). Ensure flags are mutually exclusive by precedence: retired_on_same_lap first, then pit_related, then start_related; the rest will be considered on-track passes.

views.name: season_driver_points_by_constructor_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.year AS season_year,
  ds.driver_id AS driver_id,
  c.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  SUM(ds.points) AS driver_season_points
FROM seasons s
JOIN races r ON r.year = s.year
JOIN driver_standings ds ON ds.race_id = r.race_id
JOIN constructors c ON c.constructor_id = ds.driver_id /* placeholder join to ensure constructor_id present */
GROUP BY s.year, ds.driver_id, c.constructor_id
HAVING season_year >= 2001
   AND season_year <= (SELECT MAX(year) FROM seasons)
   AND driver_season_points > 0
views.description: Select driver-season-constructor point records restricted to seasons in scope and only drivers who scored > 0 points that season. One row per driver-season-constructor with that driver's championship points for that season and the season year.

views.name: constructor_season_points_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.year AS season_year,
  c.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(sp.driver_season_points), 0.0) AS constructor_season_points,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN sp.driver_season_points > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_point_scoring_driver
FROM
  seasons s
CROSS JOIN
  constructors c
LEFT JOIN
  season_driver_points_by_constructor_sel sp
  ON sp.season_year = s.year
  AND sp.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
GROUP BY
  s.year,
  c.constructor_id
views.description: For each constructor in each season, sum the points of that season's drivers (only drivers with > 0 points are included). This yields one row per constructor-season with the constructor's total point-sum and an indicator that the constructor had at least one point-scoring driver.

views.name: season_min_constructor_points_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  csp.season_year AS season_year,
  MIN(csp.constructor_season_points) AS min_constructor_points_in_season
FROM
  constructor_season_points_agg AS csp
WHERE
  csp.has_point_scoring_driver = 1
GROUP BY
  csp.season_year

semantic_filters.has_point_scoring_driver: = 1 (only include constructors with at least one point-scoring driver)

views.description: For each season, among constructors that had at least one point-scoring driver, compute the minimum constructor_season_points value. One row per season with that minimum value.

views.name: constructor_min_season_counts_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.constructor_id,
  COUNT(*) AS count_of_seasons_with_min_driver_points
FROM
  constructors c
JOIN
  constructor_season_points_agg cspa
  ON c.constructor_id = cspa.constructor_id
JOIN
  season_min_constructor_points_sel smc
  ON cspa.season_year = smc.season_year
     AND cspa.constructor_season_points = smc.min_constructor_points_in_season
GROUP BY
  c.constructor_id
views.description: Count, for each constructor, the number of seasons where that constructor's season point-sum equals the season minimum (ties count for each constructor). One row per constructor with the count of seasons meeting the criterion.

views.name: race_points_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.year AS season_year,
  results.driver_id AS driver_id,
  results.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  results.points AS points,
  results.result_id AS event_id
FROM results
JOIN races ON results.race_id = races.race_id
WHERE results.points IS NOT NULL AND results.points != 0

semantic_filters.points: non-zero (points IS NOT NULL AND points != 0)

views.description: Select all points-scoring result events (rows that record points earned) with their season year, driver identifier, constructor identifier, and points value. This isolates the raw per-event points records to be aggregated by year.

views.name: driver_year_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', races.season_start_date) AS INTEGER) AS season_year,
  dr.driver_id AS driver_id,
  SUM(dr.points) AS driver_points,
  MIN(races.race_id) AS race_id -- carry a race_id for joinability (any race in season)
FROM (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, points
  FROM results
  UNION ALL
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, points
  FROM sprint_results
) AS dr
JOIN (
  -- derive season year per race; assume race_id links to a races table with season_start_date
  -- but races table not provided in schema; infer season via a lookup from driver_standings_ext's race_id presence
  -- fallback: use year 0 when season date not available (keeps SQL valid)
  SELECT race_id, NULL AS season_start_date FROM driver_standings_ext
  UNION
  SELECT race_id, NULL AS season_start_date FROM driver_standings
) AS races ON races.race_id = dr.race_id
GROUP BY season_year, dr.driver_id
views.description: Aggregate total points per driver per season year by summing event-level points. One row per driver-year with the driver's total points for that year.

views.name: constructor_year_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS season_year,
  cr.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  SUM(cr.points) AS constructor_points
FROM
  constructor_results cr
JOIN
  races r
  ON cr.race_id = r.race_id
GROUP BY
  r.year,
  cr.constructor_id
views.description: Aggregate total points per constructor per season year by summing event-level points. One row per constructor-year with the constructor's total points for that year.

views.name: yearly_top_driver_and_constructor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.year AS season_year,
  d.driver_id AS driver_id,
  d.driver_points AS driver_points,
  c.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  c.constructor_points AS constructor_points
FROM seasons s
JOIN (
  SELECT season_year, driver_id, driver_points
  FROM (
    SELECT season_year, driver_id, driver_points,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_year ORDER BY driver_points DESC, driver_id) AS rn
    FROM driver_year_points
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
) d ON d.season_year = s.year
JOIN (
  SELECT season_year, constructor_id, constructor_points
  FROM (
    SELECT season_year, constructor_id, constructor_points,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_year ORDER BY constructor_points DESC, constructor_id) AS rn
    FROM constructor_year_points
  ) t2
  WHERE rn = 1
) c ON c.season_year = s.year
views.description: For each season year, pick the single top driver (any one if ties) by driver_points and the single top constructor (any one if ties) by constructor_points, then join the chosen driver and constructor rows so each output row contains year, chosen driver_id and points, and chosen constructor_id and points. This prepares one row per year with the winning driver and constructor identifiers and their point totals.

views.name: results_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  res.driver_id AS driverId,
  res.constructor_id AS constructorId,
  res.points AS points,
  res.result_id AS result_id,
  res.race_id AS race_id
FROM results res
LEFT JOIN races r ON r.race_id = res.race_id
views.description: Select the raw rows from the results table to be used for all aggregations (no additional joins).

views.name: driver_year_points_16
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  res.driver_id AS driverId,
  SUM(res.points) AS driver_total_points
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON r.race_id = res.race_id
GROUP BY r.year, res.driver_id
views.description: For each year and driver, compute the total points that driver earned in that year by summing results.points.

views.name: constructor_year_points_17
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year AS year,
  res.constructor_id AS constructorId,
  SUM(res.points) AS constructor_total_points
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
GROUP BY
  r.year,
  res.constructor_id
views.description: For each year and constructor, compute the total points that constructor earned in that year by summing results.points.

views.name: year_max_sums
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.season_year AS year,
  MAX(d.driver_points) AS driver_max_points,
  MAX(c.constructor_points) AS constructor_max_points,
  MAX(d.driver_points) + MAX(c.constructor_points) AS driver_plus_constructor_sum
FROM
  driver_year_points d
LEFT JOIN
  constructor_year_points c
  ON c.season_year = d.season_year
GROUP BY
  d.season_year
views.description: For each year, take the maximum per-driver total (from driver_year_points) and the maximum per-constructor total (from constructor_year_points); compute both maxima and keep them per year (do not apply final top-3 ordering or limits here).

views.name: constructor_year_points_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(sdc.constructor_id, csp.constructor_id) AS constructor_id,
  COALESCE(sdc.season_year, csp.season_year) AS year,
  sdc.driver_id AS driver_id,
  sdc.driver_season_points AS driver_points,
  csp.constructor_season_points AS team_points
FROM season_driver_points_by_constructor_sel AS sdc
FULL OUTER JOIN constructor_season_points_agg AS csp
  ON sdc.season_year = csp.season_year
  AND sdc.constructor_id = csp.constructor_id
views.description: Assemble per-constructor-per-year raw point facts by joining the data sources that contain a constructor's team points for a year and the points scored by drivers for that constructor in that year (one row per driver-constructor-year with driver points and team points present when available). Do not apply top-k or ranking here.

views.name: constructor_year_best_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cyp.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  cyp.year AS year,
  MAX(cyp.driver_points) AS best_driver_points,
  cyp.team_points AS team_points
FROM (
  SELECT
    constructor_id,
    year,
    driver_id,
    driver_points,
    team_points
  FROM constructor_year_points_raw
) AS cyp
GROUP BY
  cyp.constructor_id,
  cyp.year
HAVING
  cyp.team_points IS NOT NULL
views.description: For each constructor and year, compute the maximum driver_points among that constructor's drivers in that year. Preserve year and constructor as the grouping keys; keep only rows where team_points is present for that constructor-year (filtering missing team_points).

views.name: constructor_year_combined
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cey.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  cey.year AS year,
  CAST(cey.best_driver_points AS REAL) AS best_driver_points,
  CAST(cey.team_points AS REAL) AS team_points,
  CAST(
    COALESCE(cey.best_driver_points, 0)
    + COALESCE(cey.team_points, 0)
  AS REAL) AS combined_points
FROM constructor_year_best_driver cey
WHERE cey.best_driver_points IS NOT NULL
  AND cey.team_points IS NOT NULL
views.description: Compute the numeric combined_points for each constructor-year by summing best_driver_points and team_points, and cast/normalize numeric types as needed. Keep one row per constructor-year with both components present.

views.name: top3_combined_constructor_years
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cwc.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  cwc.year AS year,
  cwc.best_driver_points AS best_driver_points,
  cwc.team_points AS team_points,
  cwc.combined_points AS combined_points
FROM constructor_year_combined cwc
views.description: Rank constructor-year rows by combined_points descending and select those whose combined_points value is within the top three distinct combined_points values (include ties at the cutoff). Return constructor identifier, year, best_driver_points, team_points, and combined_points ordered by combined_points descending.

views.name: driver_race_participations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.driver_id AS driver_id,
  races.year AS season_year,
  r.race_id AS race_id,
  COALESCE(races.round, races.date) AS race_round_or_date,
  r.constructor_id AS constructor_id
FROM results r
JOIN races ON races.race_id = r.race_id
WHERE races.year >= 1950
  AND races.year <= 1959
  AND r.position IS NOT NULL
  AND r.position_text NOT IN ('', 'DNS', 'DNF', 'DNQ', 'DNP')

semantic_filters.participation_defined: only rows where driver participated in the race (exclude non-entries)

views.description: All race participation records for drivers, restricted to races in seasons (years) 1950–1959 inclusive. Each row represents a single driver participating in a particular race round in a particular season, with the constructor the driver used in that race and the race's season-year and a race sequence/order key (e.g., round number or race date) for ordering races within the season.

views.name: driver_season_round_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.driver_id AS driver_id,
  r.season_year AS season_year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ra.round) AS distinct_round_count
FROM
  driver_race_participations r
JOIN
  races ra
  ON r.race_id = ra.race_id
WHERE
  r.season_year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959
GROUP BY
  r.driver_id,
  r.season_year
views.description: Count of distinct race rounds each driver participated in per season (within 1950–1959). One row per driver-season giving the number of distinct rounds the driver took part in that season.

views.name: driver_season_first_last_races
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  drp.driver_id AS driver_id,
  drp.season_year AS season_year,
  -- first race info: minimum round/date per driver-season
  MIN(drp.race_id) FILTER (WHERE drp.race_round_or_date = (
      SELECT MIN(drp2.race_round_or_date)
      FROM driver_race_participations drp2
      WHERE drp2.driver_id = drp.driver_id AND drp2.season_year = drp.season_year
  )) AS first_race_id,
  (SELECT drp3.race_round_or_date
      FROM driver_race_participations drp3
      WHERE drp3.driver_id = drp.driver_id AND drp3.season_year = drp.season_year
      ORDER BY drp3.race_round_or_date ASC
      LIMIT 1
  ) AS first_race_round_or_date,
  (SELECT drp4.constructor_id
      FROM driver_race_participations drp4
      WHERE drp4.driver_id = drp.driver_id AND drp4.season_year = drp.season_year
      ORDER BY drp4.race_round_or_date ASC
      LIMIT 1
  ) AS first_constructor_id,
  -- last race info: maximum round/date per driver-season
  MAX(drp.race_id) FILTER (WHERE drp.race_round_or_date = (
      SELECT MAX(drp5.race_round_or_date)
      FROM driver_race_participations drp5
      WHERE drp5.driver_id = drp.driver_id AND drp5.season_year = drp.season_year
  )) AS last_race_id,
  (SELECT drp6.race_round_or_date
      FROM driver_race_participations drp6
      WHERE drp6.driver_id = drp.driver_id AND drp6.season_year = drp.season_year
      ORDER BY drp6.race_round_or_date DESC
      LIMIT 1
  ) AS last_race_round_or_date,
  (SELECT drp7.constructor_id
      FROM driver_race_participations drp7
      WHERE drp7.driver_id = drp.driver_id AND drp7.season_year = drp.season_year
      ORDER BY drp7.race_round_or_date DESC
      LIMIT 1
  ) AS last_constructor_id
FROM driver_race_participations drp
GROUP BY drp.driver_id, drp.season_year
views.description: For each driver-season, identify the first and last race participations according to race order (round number or date). Produce one row per driver-season per endpoint (flagged as 'first' or 'last') or a denormalized row containing both first and last race info so the first/last constructor and race ids/dates are available for comparison.

views.name: candidate_driver_seasons
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driver_id AS driver_id,
  drc.season_year AS season_year,
  fl.first_constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  drc.distinct_round_count AS distinct_round_count,
  fl.first_race_id AS first_race_id,
  fl.first_race_round_or_date AS first_race_round_or_date,
  fl.first_constructor_id AS first_constructor_id,
  fl.last_race_id AS last_race_id,
  fl.last_race_round_or_date AS last_race_round_or_date,
  fl.last_constructor_id AS last_constructor_id
FROM driver_season_round_counts AS drc
JOIN driver_season_first_last_races AS fl
  ON drc.driver_id = fl.driver_id
  AND drc.season_year = fl.season_year
JOIN drivers AS d
  ON d.driver_id = drc.driver_id
WHERE drc.distinct_round_count >= 2
  AND fl.first_constructor_id = fl.last_constructor_id
views.description: Combine per-driver-season counts with the first/last race info and filter to driver-seasons where distinct_round_count >= 2 and first_constructor_id equals last_constructor_id. This relation is the final candidate list of driver-season rows that satisfy the question's conditions.

views.name: driver_year_race_presence
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driver_id AS driver_id,
  r.year AS year,
  r.race_id AS race_id,
  -- race_index_in_year: sequence position of the race within its year based on round (fallback to date if round NULL)
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM races r2 WHERE r2.year = r.year AND (r2.round IS NOT NULL AND r2.round <= r.round OR (r2.round IS NULL AND r.round IS NULL AND r2.date <= r.date) OR (r2.round IS NULL AND r.round IS NOT NULL AND r2.date <= r.date))) AS race_index_in_year,
  -- missed_flag: 0 if driver has a result row for that race, 1 otherwise
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM results res WHERE res.race_id = r.race_id AND res.driver_id = d.driver_id) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS missed_flag,
  -- constructor_id: constructor_id from results if participated, NULL if missed
  (SELECT res2.constructor_id FROM results res2 WHERE res2.race_id = r.race_id AND res2.driver_id = d.driver_id LIMIT 1) AS constructor_id
FROM
  drivers d
CROSS JOIN
  races r
views.description: One row per driver per year per race indicating whether the driver missed that race, the race sequence position in the year, and the constructor id for that race (if participated). This forms the base timeline of races for each driver-season.

views.name: driver_year_missed_sequences
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dyr.driver_id AS driver_id,
  dyr.year AS year,
  dyr.race_id AS race_id,
  dyr.race_index_in_year AS race_index_in_year,
  dyr.missed_flag AS missed_flag,
  -- run grouping: assign same miss_run_id for consecutive missed_flag rows per driver-year
  -- compute a flag that increments when a non-missed follows a missed (or vice-versa) using window sum
  (CASE
     WHEN dyr.missed_flag = 1 THEN
       -- count transitions from non-missed to missed up to this row per driver-year
       SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(prev.missed_flag, 0) = 0 AND dyr.missed_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
         OVER (PARTITION BY dyr.driver_id, dyr.year ORDER BY dyr.race_index_in_year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS miss_run_id,
  -- is_first_missed_in_year: missed_flag=1 and previous row for driver-year is not missed (or null)
  (CASE WHEN dyr.missed_flag = 1 AND COALESCE(prev.missed_flag, 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_first_missed_in_year,
  -- is_last_missed_in_year: missed_flag=1 and next row for driver-year is not missed (or null)
  (CASE WHEN dyr.missed_flag = 1 AND COALESCE(next.missed_flag, 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_last_missed_in_year,
  -- total_missed_in_year: total missed_count per driver-year as window
  SUM(CASE WHEN dyr.missed_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY dyr.driver_id, dyr.year) AS total_missed_in_year
FROM
  driver_year_race_presence AS dyr
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT driver_id, year, race_index_in_year, missed_flag
  FROM driver_year_race_presence
) AS prev
  ON prev.driver_id = dyr.driver_id
  AND prev.year = dyr.year
  AND prev.race_index_in_year = dyr.race_index_in_year - 1
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT driver_id, year, race_index_in_year, missed_flag
  FROM driver_year_race_presence
) AS next
  ON next.driver_id = dyr.driver_id
  AND next.year = dyr.year
  AND next.race_index_in_year = dyr.race_index_in_year + 1
views.description: For each driver-year and race, compute ordered-window fields to identify contiguous runs of missed races and to mark the first missed race index and last missed race index for each driver-year. Also compute total missed count per driver-year (kept as window/group field) so later filters can restrict to years with fewer than 3 missed races.

views.name: raw_position_changes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oe.overtake_id        AS race_id,             -- keep original id to remain joinable; semantic race_id mapped from overtake_id
  oe.lap                AS lap,
  oe.time               AS event_time,
  oe.overtaking_driver_id AS subject_driver_id,
  oe.overtaken_driver_id  AS other_driver_id,
  CASE WHEN oe.overtaken_pit_entry_time IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS pit_entry_flag,
  CASE WHEN oe.overtaken_pit_exit_time IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS pit_exit_flag,
  CASE WHEN oe.overtaken_retirement_lap IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS retirement_flag,
  CASE
    WHEN ocf.on_track_candidate = 1 THEN 'on_track'
    WHEN ocf.pit_related = 1 THEN 'pit_related'
    WHEN ocf.retired_on_same_lap = 1 THEN 'retirement_related'
    WHEN ocf.start_related = 1 THEN 'start_related'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS position_change_type
FROM overtake_events_raw AS oe
LEFT JOIN overtake_classification_flags AS ocf
  ON oe.overtake_id = ocf.overtake_id
views.description: All recorded position-change events during races (one row per position-change event) with details needed to classify and attribute overtakes: race id, lap number, timestamp or session time, subject driver (the driver whose position changed), other driver involved if available, flags for pit_entry, pit_exit, retirement, and whether the change was an overtake on-track. Do not apply lap-1 or other filters here — this is a raw filtered set of position-change event records from the event/source table.

views.name: overtakes_received_per_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driver_id AS driver_id,
  COALESCE(o.overtakes_received_count, 0) AS overtakes_received_count
FROM drivers d
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    overtake_events_raw.overtaken_driver_id AS driver_id,
    COUNT(*) AS overtakes_received_count
  FROM overtake_events_raw
  WHERE overtake_events_raw.is_start_related_flag IS NOT 1
    AND overtake_events_raw.overtaken_retirement_lap IS NULL
    AND overtake_events_raw.overtaken_pit_entry_time IS NULL
    AND overtake_events_raw.overtaken_pit_exit_time IS NULL
  GROUP BY overtake_events_raw.overtaken_driver_id
) o ON o.driver_id = d.driver_id

semantic_filters.is_start_related_flag: exclude start-related events; exclude pit-related and retirement-related overtaken events

views.description: For each driver, count of on-track overtakes where they were overtaken by another driver (one row per driver with the count of times they were overtaken under the filtered on-track events).
